answer: At each dawn, agents could escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake before joining a market, then earn reputation only through tasks whose results are checked by randomly selected peers with their own established stake. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting into a spiral of accounts does not multiply influence; each account must lock more capital and risk slashing when caught colluding. Even an attacker using shale-like cheap hardware faces that financial cost, while honest agents can build trust over time.
